$comment: Wave 9 statistics register (W9-13). Generated from the proof library of the sales strategy (section 1.6) on 2026-10-14. A page quotes a figure only as written here, cites its source line, and records the source in its own .astro-magazine/sources/wp-NN.json with source_id set to the ST id. The figures describe the market, never WE's results (C-13); no page claims that WE improves survival, shortens time to a raise or makes a company fundable (C-05, C-16). Owner: WP-51, handed to WP-57.

statistics.statistic: 77.9% of new U.S. establishments were still operating after one year. About 1 in 5 close in year one
statistics.source: BLS Business Employment Dynamics, Table 7 (group opened in the year to March 2024)

statistics.statistic: 51.4% survive five years (2020 group). The 1994 to 2022 average is 49.2%. "About half are gone by year five"
statistics.source: BLS BED Table 7; SBA Advocacy FAQ 2026, Q9

statistics.statistic: 34.7% survive ten years (2015 group); the average is 33.9%. "About a third are still operating at year ten"
statistics.source: BLS BED Table 7; SBA Advocacy FAQ 2026

statistics.statistic: The odds improve with time: 69.5% of five-year survivors reach year ten, and 76.1% of ten-year survivors reach year fifteen
GEM counts a business as "established" only after 42 months (3.5 years) of paying wages
statistics.source: GEM U.S. 2019/2020 Report, p. 26; Babson GEM USA 2026

statistics.statistic: A record 5,671,836 U.S. business applications in 2025, the highest year since the series began
statistics.source: Census Business Formation Statistics (sum of monthly, not seasonally adjusted values)
statistics.status: DERIVED. The Census revision on 2026-11-12 may change it

statistics.statistic: Of 2021 applications, 5.8% became employer businesses within a year and 7.5% within two
Applicants that hired took 2.29 quarters on average to reach first payroll (2021), against 1.48 in 2005
The median VC-backed company is 2.8 years old at its Series A and 7.4 at Series D. The median gap from seed to Series A is 2.0 years
statistics.source: Carta, State of Private Markets Q1 2026
statistics.status: VERIFIED. Applies to VC-backed companies only

statistics.statistic: Three-month programs last about 3 months. Incubators last 1 to 5 years
Among VC-backed startups that shut down, 70% cited running out of capital and 43% cited poor product-market fit
statistics.status: VERIFIED. VC-backed only; multiple answers allowed

statistics.statistic: About a third of nascent ventures ever become a profitable firm
One study found that firms leaving an incubator showed lower survival for up to three years after leaving
statistics.status: VERIFIED. Quote it as "one study" and never as a WE result

statistics.statistic: Research on intensive early-stage programs found that the active ingredient was "broad, intensive, and paced consultation", and that only some programs had it
Funding and desk space alone showed no measurable effect. Structured entrepreneurship training bundled with them did
The average founder of the fastest-growing 0.1% of U.S. startups was 45 at founding. The average for all hiring startups was 41.9
A 50-year-old founder is 1.8 times as likely as a 30-year-old to build a top-growth company
Founders with 3+ years in the same industry reach top-0.1% growth at about twice the rate of founders without (0.26% vs 0.12%)
Founders with a prior success succeed 30% of the time. First-timers succeed 21% of the time, and founders whose last venture failed 22%
51.3% of U.S. employer-business owners have owned a business before, and 76.3% are 45 or older
Immigrants start businesses at twice the U.S.-born rate (0.60% vs 0.30% of adults a month, 2025), and are 28.2% of new entrepreneurs
55% of U.S. billion-dollar startups had at least one immigrant founder (319 of 582)
Immigrant workers founded firms at an 80% higher rate than U.S.-born workers
In 2025, 57% of white-owned firms got the full financing they sought, against 32% of Black-owned and 33% of Hispanic-owned firms
statistics.source: Federal Reserve Small Business Credit Survey

statistics.statistic: Latino adults start businesses at the highest monthly rate of any group (0.53%), yet Hispanic-owned firms are 8.4% of employer businesses
statistics.status: VERIFIED. This shows a conversion gap, not its cause

statistics.statistic: Women are 39.9% of new entrepreneurs and own 22.9% of employer firms solely. Measured properly, women-owned ventures perform as well as men's
statistics.status: VERIFIED; the performance finding is SECONDARY

statistics.statistic: More than 1 in 5 new U.S. entrepreneurs (22.8%) is aged 55 to 64, up from about 1 in 7 (14.8%) in 1996
More than 1 in 5 Americans aged 18 to 34 are starting or running a new business, yet only 5.7% of employer-business owners are under 35
About 1 in 6 new entrepreneurs (16.7%) start out of necessity. The share jumped to 30.2% in 2020
Only 6.8% of established employer-business owners say "couldn't find a job" was a very important reason for owning
The median small business held 17.6 days of cash buffer in 2025
Losing a first-year employee has a large negative effect on a firm's size for at least 10 years
Firms aged 0 to 5 years were fully approved for financing 48% of the time, against 63% for firms aged 21 or more
Each year a business survives, its odds of surviving the next year rise: from 79.6% in year one to 94.4% in year nine (2013 group)
Information-sector (including software) establishments: 71.6% survive year one and 45.7% survive five years. Professional and technical services: 74.5% and 50.8%
Survivors grow: in the 2010 group, the average survivor went from 4.5 employees at opening to 11.3 at year ten
Founders consistently underestimate how long market validation takes. One 2011 study put it at 2 to 3 times longer than expected
statistics.status: SECONDARY. Say "founders underestimate" and do not present it as a measured duration

statistics.statistic: Black-owned startups start with less capital and stay smaller for their first eight years
56% of veteran business owners have owned a business before
56.3% of new establishments survive three years (2022 group); 65.9% survive two (2023 group)
statistics.status: VERIFIED. The 2022 group opened in a pandemic-era surge

statistics.statistic: Majority immigrant-owned firms were fully approved for financing 44% of the time, against 54% for other firms (2025)

neverUse: Any "incubated firms survive X% more" figure.
"12% more likely to survive with an adviser".
"51% of Gen Z want to start a business".
Exact female-founder VC decimals (say "about 1 to 2%" if needed at all).
"37% had no revenue in year one".
Either figure for the GEM established-ownership rate (sources conflict).
The "studio companies reach Series A in 25 months" figure.
